articles.title: What’s the future of the Western Sahara conflict?
UN's peacekeeping mission in disputed Western Sahara ends after 35 years

events.summary: The United Nations is terminating its 35-year peacekeeping mission in Western Sahara. The extension was blocked jointly by the United States and Russia.
events.why: Ending a decades-long UN peacekeeping mandate leaves a security vacuum that significantly raises the risk of renewed armed conflict in Western Sahara.

articles.title: Binance users withdraw $3.6bn after largest-ever crypto hack
Binance resumes customer withdrawals after record $6.3bn hack

events.summary: Binance experienced a record cyber hack linked to a North Korean group, prompting users to withdraw billions of dollars. The exchange temporarily froze transactions before resuming customer withdrawals.
events.why: A multi-billion dollar theft from the world's largest crypto exchange threatens market liquidity and underscores significant state-sponsored cybersecurity threats to financial infrastructure.

articles.title: Uganda begins withdrawing troops from Somalia after 20 years
Uganda begins withdrawing troops from Somalia after two decades

events.summary: Uganda has started pulling its troops out of Somalia after two decades of involvement. The forces had been supporting Somalia against an insurgency led by the al-Shabab militant group since 2007.
events.why: The withdrawal of a primary troop contributor risks destabilizing the Horn of Africa and shifting the security balance against al-Shabab.

articles.title: Thousands of European troops to rehearse Ukraine deployment in event of peace

events.summary: Thousands of European troops will participate in rehearsals for a potential deployment to Ukraine in the event of peace. Officials emphasized that these forces would not take part in offensive operations.
events.why: Planning for European peacekeeping forces marks a significant structural commitment to post-conflict security guarantees in Eastern Europe.

articles.title: Trump to remove Rwanda and South Africa from US trade deal
US to drop South Africa, Rwanda from duty-free trade initiative

events.summary: The US plans to remove Rwanda and South Africa from a duty-free trade initiative. This decision follows US Treasury sanctions on Rwanda's defence ministry a week earlier.
events.why: Losing duty-free access directly impacts export revenues and trade dynamics for two significant African economies while signaling shifts in US diplomatic strategy.

articles.title: If hackers can take control of a supermarket freezer, how vulnerable is other tech?
Who is hacking Europe’s supermarket fridges and freezers, and why?

events.summary: Dozens of shops across multiple European countries suffered a cyber-attack affecting their fridges and freezers. The attack has raised broader concerns regarding vulnerabilities in retail technology.
events.why: It demonstrates a novel attack vector targeting commercial IoT and cold-chain infrastructure that could disrupt retail food distribution.

articles.title: Man guilty of stealing cash from farm owned by South African president

events.summary: A man was convicted of stealing cash from a farm owned by South African President Cyril Ramaphosa. The incident forms part of the ongoing "Farmgate" scandal affecting Ramaphosa's presidency.
events.why: Legal developments in the Farmgate scandal carry political consequences for the leadership and stability of the South African government.

articles.title: Ryanair says it may freeze workers' pay and raise airfares

events.summary: Ryanair announced potential wage freezes and ticket price increases due to escalating operating costs. The carrier cited a potential €2bn surge in fuel costs by 2028 tied to regional conflict involving the US, Israel, and Iran.
events.why: Fuel cost pressures on Europe's largest budget airline signal broader economic strain on commercial aviation and consumer travel costs.

articles.title: Plane may have broken apart ahead of deadly Florida jet crash, say investigators

events.summary: Investigators suggest a plane may have broken apart prior to a fatal crash in Florida. The National Transportation Safety Board noted weather may have played a role, though the exact cause remains undetermined.
events.why: While a tragic aviation accident, it is currently a localized incident pending findings that might imply broader fleet-wide safety issues.

articles.title: Fake nuclear warning from hacked app sparks unease but not panic in Ukraine

events.summary: A hacked mobile application broadcast a fake nuclear warning across Ukraine, causing unease rather than mass panic. Many citizens doubted the messages due to years of experience with attacks.
events.why: It highlights cyber threats targeting civilian warning infrastructure to cause psychological disruption during active warfare.

articles.title: Five arrested after South African farmer shot and tortured

events.summary: Five individuals were arrested following the shooting and torture of a 50-year-old South African farmer. The assault occurred amidst discredited rhetoric from right-wing groups alleging white genocide.
events.why: The violent crime touches on sensitive racial and political tensions in South Africa, frequently exploited for political agitation.
